items.title: Customs broker's AI document extraction and cross-check tool for import shipments
items.body:
CLIENT: Company A, Navi Mumbai. Freight forwarder and customs broker at Nhava Sheva. 85 staff, revenue ₹60–75 crore a year, a documentation team of 14.

TODAY: Importers email invoices, packing lists and bills of lading as PDFs, scans or photos. Executives retype the data into an Excel checklist, then into the customs filing software. Seniors raise doubts in a WhatsApp group.

THE PROBLEM: Assumptions: 1,100 shipments a month, 45 minutes of data entry each, ₹350 per staff hour. 1,100 × 0.75 h × 12 = 9,900 hours = ₹34.65 lakh a year. 3% of shipments have an error that forces an amended Bill of Entry or port delay: 13,200 × 3% = 396 cases × ₹9,000 (fees, demurrage, staff time) = ₹35.64 lakh. Total ₹70.29 lakh a year.

USERS: Documentation executives (enter and confirm data), the documentation manager (approves), and importers (send documents and answer queries). The Managing Director signs the deal.

THE ASK: My team spends half the day typing what is already written in a PDF. I want to drop in a shipment's documents and get the data out ready to check. It must catch mismatches, like weights that differ across documents. I don't want to change our filing software.

MUST HAVE:
- Shipment record with upload of invoice, packing list and bill of lading
- AI extraction of parties, invoice number and date, currency, Incoterm, line items with HSN, packages, weights and containers
- Review screen with the document beside the fields, low-confidence fields highlighted
- Cross-checks: invoice total vs line sum, packages and weights across all three documents
- Export in the filing software's Excel import layout, and a shipment status list
- Edit history and accuracy report per field and supplier

CORE BUILD: Software Engineering candidates must ship this slice end to end, in about 6 to 8 screens: shipment list, document upload, AI extraction, side-by-side review with cross-checks, and CSV export. Roles: documentation executive and manager. AI: field extraction with confidence scores. Hard part: reliable cross-checks across three documents. Mock payments, messages and outside systems, and seed from the sample data. The rest of MUST HAVE is optional depth.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Filing on the customs portal
- HSN classification or duty calculation
- Customer tracking portal

AI OR AUTOMATION: A vision AI model reads each document and returns fields with confidence scores. When it is wrong: low-confidence fields and fields in a failed cross-check must be confirmed by a person, and nothing exports until they are cleared. Corrections are logged to show accuracy per field and supplier. Unreadable pages go to manual entry.

CONSTRAINTS: Client prices are confidential: host in India, use role-based access, and use an AI provider that does not train on client data. Importer contacts are personal data under the DPDP Act 2023. Scans are often skewed or bilingual. Desktop use.

DESIGN: The client values good, minimal design: clean layouts, white space, a restrained palette and clear type, with nothing on screen that lacks a purpose. Design counts as much as features. The review screen is used all day: show the document and fields side by side, make uncertain fields obvious at a glance, and keep every action one click away.

BUDGET AND TIME: ₹7.5 lakh, 6 weeks. Success: entry time per shipment from 45 to under 15 minutes; 95% field accuracy on 200 past shipments; amended Bills of Entry halved in 3 months.

items.title: Diagnostic lab chain's report-delivery portal for patients and referring doctors
items.body:
CLIENT: Company A, Vijayawada. 6 labs and 38 collection centres in coastal Andhra Pradesh. 260 staff, revenue ₹45–55 crore a year.

TODAY: A desktop lab information system (LIS) produces signed PDF reports. Front-desk staff send them one by one on WhatsApp from 9 shared phones. Patients call or walk in to ask if reports are ready. Referring doctors get printouts by hand.

THE PROBLEM: Assumptions: 2,000 patients a day, 360 days. 30% call or visit about status: 600 × 4 minutes = 40 staff hours a day × 360 = 14,400 hours × ₹250 = ₹36 lakh a year. 40% of reports are still printed and delivered: 7,20,000 × 40% = 2,88,000 × ₹12 = ₹34.56 lakh. Total ₹70.56 lakh a year, plus about 15 reports a month sent to the wrong number.

USERS: Patients and families (mobile), referring doctors, and front-desk staff. The founder-CEO signs the deal.

THE ASK: Patients should never have to call us about a report. When the pathologist signs, the patient should get a safe link automatically. Referring doctors should see their patients' reports in one place. Many patients are elderly and read Telugu, so add a short plain explanation.

MUST HAVE:
- Patient login by mobile and OTP, listing orders with status and PDF download
- Automatic WhatsApp or SMS with an expiring link when a report is signed, fed by the LIS export folder
- Referring doctor view of the last 90 days of their patients' reports
- Plain-language summary of out-of-range values in English, Telugu and Hindi
- Front-desk console to find a patient, resend links and see delivery status, plus an access log
- Delivery and access report for the operations head

CORE BUILD: Software Engineering candidates must ship this slice end to end, in about 6 to 8 screens: LIS CSV import, automatic report link on sign-off, patient OTP portal with report view, plain-language summary, and front-desk resend. Roles: patient and front-desk staff. AI: summary of out-of-range values. Hard part: secure expiring links with OTP. Mock payments, messages and outside systems, and seed from the sample data. The rest of MUST HAVE is optional depth.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Changes to the LIS
- Online test booking and payment
- Home-collection scheduling

AI OR AUTOMATION: Delivery is automated. AI writes the summaries, but out-of-range flags come from rules using the report's reference ranges. When the AI is wrong: summaries use locked templates for the 30 most common tests, always link to the full report, and can be flagged by patients. Critical values get no summary and create a callback task for staff. A pathologist reviews 50 summaries a week.

CONSTRAINTS: Health data is sensitive personal data under the DPDP Act 2023: consent at registration, hosting in India, access logs. Links expire in 72 hours and need OTP to reopen. Patients use low-end phones on weak data, so pages must be light. One number often covers a whole family.

DESIGN: The client values good, minimal design: clean layouts, white space, a restrained palette and clear type, with nothing on screen that lacks a purpose. Design counts as much as features. Many patients are elderly on small phones: large text, one clear action per screen, and a report page that reads well in Telugu.

BUDGET AND TIME: ₹6.5 lakh, 6 weeks. Success: status calls down 60% in 3 months; 80% of reports delivered digitally; printing halved; no report opened by the wrong person.

items.title: Mid-size hospital's cashless claims and TPA tracking workspace
items.body:
CLIENT: Company A, Nashik. Multispeciality hospital with 180 beds, 520 staff, revenue ₹110–130 crore a year. 60% of inpatients are cashless insured. An insurance desk of 9 handles claims.

TODAY: The desk types pre-authorisation forms, scans doctors' notes and emails them to over 20 insurers and TPAs, each with its own format. Status lives in Excel. Queries come by email and doctors are chased on WhatsApp.

THE PROBLEM: Assumptions: 650 cashless admissions a month at ₹85,000 average. 7,800 claims = ₹66.3 crore billed a year. Avoidable deductions from missing documents: 0.8% = ₹53.04 lakh. 30% of claims get a query: 2,340 × 1.5 hours × ₹300 = ₹10.53 lakh. Total ₹63.57 lakh a year, plus patients waiting 4.5 hours for discharge approval.

USERS: Insurance desk executives, the desk head, and treating doctors. The CFO signs the deal.

THE ASK: We lose money because a document was missing, not because treatment was wrong. I want every claim in one place with a checklist showing what is missing before we send it. When a TPA sends a query I want to see what they want and by when.

MUST HAVE:
- Claim file per admission with a status timeline (pre-auth, query, approved, final bill, settled)
- Document checklist per insurer and procedure, set by an admin, showing gaps before submission
- AI sorting of uploads into checklist slots and pre-filling of pre-auth fields
- Query inbox where AI summarises TPA emails and starts a reply countdown
- Merged PDF packet per TPA, and a dashboard of pending approvals and deductions by reason
- Doctor approval of notes from a phone link

CORE BUILD: Software Engineering candidates must ship this slice end to end, in about 6 to 8 screens: claim file with status timeline, admin checklist per insurer, uploads sorted into checklist slots, gap view, and query inbox with countdown. Roles: desk executive and desk head. AI: document sorting and field pre-fill. Hard part: checklist rules per insurer and procedure. Mock payments, messages and outside systems, and seed from the sample data. The rest of MUST HAVE is optional depth.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Integration with insurer portals or claims exchanges
- Changes to billing or the hospital system
- Government scheme claims

AI OR AUTOMATION: AI classifies documents, extracts key fields and summarises queries. When it is wrong: each pre-filled field shows its source snippet and needs a click to confirm, misfiled documents can be dragged to the right slot, and summaries always show the original email below. Nothing is sent to a TPA automatically.

CONSTRAINTS: Patient records are sensitive personal data under the DPDP Act 2023: role-based access, audit logs, hosting in India. IRDAI expects insurers to decide cashless requests in 1 hour and discharge in 3 hours, so the hospital's own delays must be timed. Doctors' notes are often handwritten scans.

DESIGN: The client values good, minimal design: clean layouts, white space, a restrained palette and clear type, with nothing on screen that lacks a purpose. Design counts as much as features. The claim file must show at a glance what is missing and what is overdue, without the desk scrolling through clutter.

BUDGET AND TIME: ₹8.5 lakh, 7 weeks. Success: avoidable deductions down 40% in 6 months; discharge approval wait from 4.5 to under 2.5 hours; 90% of queries answered the same day.

items.title: MSME lender's field collections app with AI prioritisation
items.body:
CLIENT: Company A, Indore. RBI-registered NBFC lending to small manufacturers and traders. Loan book ₹320 crore across 4,800 loans, 140 staff including 55 field collection officers, revenue ₹65–75 crore a year.

TODAY: The loan system exports an overdue list to Excel each morning. Branch managers send names to officers on WhatsApp, and outcomes come back the same way. Promises to pay live in notebooks. Head office rebuilds the picture in Excel weekly.

THE PROBLEM: Assumptions: 450 loans a month fall 1–30 days past due (DPD). 22% roll to 31–60 DPD (99); the target is 16% (72), saving 27 a month, 324 a year. With ₹5 lakh average outstanding, 20% of rolled loans turning NPA and 35% loss: 0.20 × 0.35 × ₹5 lakh = ₹35,000 per rolled loan. 324 × ₹35,000 = ₹1.134 crore. Manual reporting: 55 officers × 1.5 hours × 300 days × ₹200 = ₹49.5 lakh. Total ₹1.63 crore a year.

USERS: Field collection officers (phone), branch managers, and the head of collections. The CEO signs the deal.

THE ASK: My officers start and end the day on WhatsApp, and I can't see what happened in between. Each officer should open an app and know which borrowers matter most today, and why. I need roll rates by branch without waiting for Friday's Excel.

MUST HAVE:
- Daily CSV import of overdue loans, auto-assigned by pincode and workload
- Officer app: prioritised list, call and map buttons, and outcome logging (paid, promise, not reachable, dispute) with GPS
- Promise-to-pay reminders to borrower and officer
- AI priority score per loan with the top three reasons
- AI-drafted Hindi or English reminders from approved templates, plus a manager dashboard of roll rates and broken promises
- Officer activity log with visit locations

CORE BUILD: Software Engineering candidates must ship this slice end to end, in about 6 to 8 screens: overdue CSV import and assignment, officer priority list, outcome logging, promise tracker, and manager roll-rate view. Roles: field officer and branch manager. AI: priority score with reasons. Hard part: offline logging with sync, and the 8 am to 7 pm contact block. Mock payments, messages and outside systems, and seed from the sample data. The rest of MUST HAVE is optional depth.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Cash receipts and payment links
- Legal notices
- Auto-dialler or voice bot

AI OR AUTOMATION: A model scores loans on DPD, payment and promise history and amount; AI drafts reminders. When the score is wrong: it is advisory, managers can reorder lists, and a weekly back-test compares scores with actual payments. When a draft is wrong: it comes only from approved templates, a word filter blocks threatening language, and nothing sends without the officer's tap.

CONSTRAINTS: RBI rules on recovery forbid harassment and limit borrower contact to 8 am to 7 pm, so the app must block contact outside that window and record every attempt. Borrower data is personal data under the DPDP Act 2023. Officers use low-end phones with weak signal, so logging must work offline. Hindi interface.

DESIGN: The client values good, minimal design: clean layouts, white space, a restrained palette and clear type, with nothing on screen that lacks a purpose. Design counts as much as features. Officers use the app in the field with one hand: big tap targets, a short list, and an outcome logged in three taps.

BUDGET AND TIME: ₹9 lakh, 8 weeks. Success: roll rate from 22% to 16% in 4 months; 95% of visits logged the same day; weekly Excel stopped.

items.title: Auto-component maker's RFQ-to-quote costing web app
items.body:
CLIENT: Company A, Chakan, Pune. Machined and forged parts for two-wheeler, tractor and Tier-1 customers. 320 staff, revenue ₹140–160 crore a year, an estimation team of 6.

TODAY: RFQs arrive by email with drawing PDFs and Excel part lists. Estimators cost each part in a large Excel template: material, routing, cycle times, machine hour rates, overheads, packing and freight. Rates are copied by hand from an old ERP. Past quotes are hard to find.

THE PROBLEM: Assumptions: 60 RFQs a month, 5 parts each, 2.5 estimator hours per part at ₹450. 720 × 5 × 2.5 = 9,000 hours = ₹40.5 lakh a year. Turnaround is 9 working days against the 4 customers expect, and 5% of RFQs (36 a year) are lost to late replies, each worth ₹20 lakh of annual sales at 12% contribution: 36 × ₹2.4 lakh = ₹86.4 lakh. Total ₹1.27 crore a year.

USERS: Estimators, the sales head (approves and sends), and the plant head (checks routings). The Managing Director signs the deal.

THE ASK: We lose orders because our quote reaches the customer a week late. I want an estimator to open an RFQ with part details already filled in and finish costing in an hour. Rates must come from one master, and each quote must remember the rates it used. I also want to find what we quoted for a similar part last year.

MUST HAVE:
- RFQ register with due dates, owners and status (estimating, sent, won, lost with reason)
- Costing screen: material, weights, routing with cycle times and hour rates, scrap, overhead, freight and margin, priced at 2–3 volumes
- Rate masters with effective dates, so old quotes keep old rates
- AI intake from the RFQ email, Excel list and drawing title block, with suggested routings
- Approval step, PDF quote with cost breakup, and search of past quotes
- Import of past quotes from Excel

CORE BUILD: Software Engineering candidates must ship this slice end to end, in about 6 to 8 screens: RFQ register, part costing screen, rate masters with effective dates, approval, and PDF quote. Roles: estimator and sales head. AI: RFQ intake extraction. Hard part: costing formulas at several volumes with versioned rates. Mock payments, messages and outside systems, and seed from the sample data. The rest of MUST HAVE is optional depth.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- CAD or 3D model analysis
- ERP integration
- Supplier portal

AI OR AUTOMATION: AI extracts RFQ data and suggests routings from past parts. All cost maths uses fixed formulas, never AI. When AI is wrong: every pre-filled value shows its source and needs estimator acceptance, and routing suggestions show the past part they came from. Quotes above ₹25 lakh annual value need sales head approval.

CONSTRAINTS: Drawings are under customer NDAs: named-user access only, and no AI service that trains on submitted data. Prices in ₹ with GST shown separately. Desktop use. About 1,400 past quote rows must be imported from Excel.

DESIGN: The client values good, minimal design: clean layouts, white space, a restrained palette and clear type, with nothing on screen that lacks a purpose. Design counts as much as features. Estimators live in the costing screen: a dense but calm layout with clear numbers, aligned columns and no decoration.

BUDGET AND TIME: ₹8 lakh, 7 weeks. Success: turnaround from 9 to 4 working days; estimator time per part from 2.5 to 1 hour; every quote traceable to its rates.

items.title: Real estate developer's AI lead-response and site-visit booking assistant
items.body:
CLIENT: Company A, Ahmedabad. Residential developer with 2 live projects (420 apartments, 2 and 3 BHK, ₹65 lakh to ₹1.2 crore). 60 staff including 11 in sales, annual bookings ₹180–220 crore.

TODAY: Leads come from property portals, social media ads, the website and a hoarding phone number, and land in an inbox and an Excel sheet. A telecaller calls them the next morning. Site visits are fixed on WhatsApp and nobody records who came.

THE PROBLEM: Assumptions: 3,000 leads a month from ₹30 lakh of monthly ad and portal spend, ₹1,000 per lead. Median first response is 14 hours, and 35% of leads are never reached within 48 hours. 3,000 × 35% = 1,050 wasted leads × ₹1,000 = ₹10.5 lakh a month, or ₹1.26 crore a year. Only 6% of leads visit a site.

USERS: Home buyers (mostly on phones), sales executives and the sales head. The Director of sales and marketing signs the deal.

THE ASK: We pay for every lead and then let a third of them go cold. I want every enquiry answered within two minutes, at any hour, in the buyer's language. The assistant should answer basic questions, learn what they want and book a site visit in a real free slot. Serious buyers should go to a named salesperson with the chat history.

MUST HAVE:
- One lead list from all sources, with source tags and duplicate checks
- AI chat assistant (web chat now, WhatsApp later) in English, Hindi or Gujarati that answers from a fact sheet and asks budget and needs
- Site-visit booking against free slots, with location pin and reminders 1 day and 2 hours before
- Handoff to a named executive with a chat summary
- Dashboard of response time, visits, show-up rate and cost per visit by source
- Admin editor for the fact sheet and visit slots

CORE BUILD: Software Engineering candidates must ship this slice end to end, in about 6 to 8 screens: lead list with duplicate check, AI chat from the fact sheet, site-visit booking with reminders, handoff, and source dashboard. Roles: buyer and sales executive. AI: chat assistant with a booking tool. Hard part: booking only real free slots, with no double booking. Mock payments, messages and outside systems, and seed from the sample data. The rest of MUST HAVE is optional depth.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Full CRM replacement
- Booking payments and allotment letters
- Outbound voice calling

AI OR AUTOMATION: The assistant is an AI agent with a booking tool. When it is wrong: it can only state facts from the sales head's fact sheet; if a fact is missing it says a person will confirm and hands off; it never quotes a final price or discount. Buyers can ask for a person at any time, and the sales head reviews flagged chats daily.

CONSTRAINTS: Under RERA, promotional messages must show the project registration number and make no claims beyond registered details. Buyer numbers are personal data under the DPDP Act 2023: contact only with consent and honour opt-outs. WhatsApp business messages need opt-in templates.

DESIGN: The client values good, minimal design: clean layouts, white space, a restrained palette and clear type, with nothing on screen that lacks a purpose. Design counts as much as features. The chat and booking flow should feel calm and premium, in keeping with the price of the homes.

BUDGET AND TIME: ₹6 lakh, 6 weeks. Success: median first response under 5 minutes; leads not reached in 48 hours from 35% to under 5%; lead-to-visit rate from 6% to 8% in 3 months.

items.title: Coaching institute's fee tracking system and parent portal
items.body:
CLIENT: Company A, Jaipur. Engineering and medical entrance coaching, 4 centres, 2,600 students, 140 staff, revenue ₹30–34 crore a year. Average fee ₹1.2 lakh a year, paid in 3 or 4 instalments.

TODAY: Centres record receipts in a desktop fee software and post totals to Tally. Due dates sit in an Excel sheet per centre. Staff phone parents to remind them, and parents call to ask balances. Test scores go out as PDFs in WhatsApp groups. Refunds are worked out by hand.

THE PROBLEM: Assumptions: 2,600 × ₹1.2 lakh = ₹31.2 crore billed a year. 2% is never collected because follow-up is late and uneven: ₹62.4 lakh. 12% of instalment value arrives over 60 days late. 8 accounts staff spend half their time chasing dues: 4 full-time equivalents × ₹4.2 lakh = ₹16.8 lakh. Total ₹79.2 lakh a year.

USERS: Parents (mobile), students, and centre accounts staff. The founder-director signs the deal.

THE ASK: Parents should know what they owe and when, without calling us. Reminders should go out on their own and stop the moment someone pays. I want one view of dues across all centres, by batch. Refunds must follow our written policy, not someone's calculator.

MUST HAVE:
- Fee ledger per student: plan, instalments, discounts, payments, balance and days overdue
- Parent portal with OTP login: dues, receipts, attendance and test scores
- Automatic Hindi or English reminders before, on and after each due date, stopping on payment
- Payment link per instalment (gateway test mode) that marks it paid
- Pro-rata refund calculator, and an accounts dashboard by centre and batch with ageing and Tally export
- Bulk upload of attendance and test scores per batch

CORE BUILD: Software Engineering candidates must ship this slice end to end, in about 6 to 8 screens: fee ledger, parent portal with dues and pay link, reminders that stop on payment, refund calculator, and dues dashboard. Roles: parent and accounts executive. AI: dropout-risk flag. Hard part: instalment and pro-rata refund rules. Mock payments, messages and outside systems, and seed from the sample data. The rest of MUST HAVE is optional depth.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Video lectures or a learning platform
- Timetables
- Admissions CRM

AI OR AUTOMATION: Reminders and payment matching are automated. An AI flag marks students at risk of dropping out from missed instalments, falling attendance and test trends. When it is wrong: the flag only creates a counsellor call task, never a fee action or parent message, and counsellors mark false flags. Unmatched payments go to an accounts queue instead of marking anything paid.

CONSTRAINTS: The Ministry of Education's 2024 coaching guidelines require a published refund policy and a pro-rata refund within 10 days when a student leaves. Most students are minors, so the DPDP Act 2023 needs verifiable parental consent. Receipts must show GST. Parents use low-end phones; Hindi is required.

DESIGN: The client values good, minimal design: clean layouts, white space, a restrained palette and clear type, with nothing on screen that lacks a purpose. Design counts as much as features. Parents should understand their dues in five seconds: amount, due date and a pay button, nothing more.

BUDGET AND TIME: ₹6 lakh, 6 weeks. Success: value over 60 days late from 12% to 6% in two terms; parent calls about dues down 70%; month-end reconciliation from 4 days to 1.

items.title: Knitwear exporter's production order-tracking app with buyer view
items.body:
CLIENT: Company A, Tiruppur. Knitwear exporter to UK and EU buyers. 3 own units plus subcontracted printing and washing, about 900 workers, an office team of 35, revenue ₹95–110 crore a year.

TODAY: Merchandisers track orders in a large Excel sheet, updated by phoning unit supervisors. Each order's time-and-action (TNA) plan lives in another sheet. Buyers email for status and photos; samples and defects are shared on WhatsApp.

THE PROBLEM: Assumptions: 500 orders a year at ₹21 lakh average. 8% ship late (40). 15 need air freight instead of sea at ₹3.5 lakh extra: ₹52.5 lakh. The other 25 take a 5% discount: 25 × ₹1.05 lakh = ₹26.25 lakh. 12 merchandisers chase status 2 hours a day: 7,200 hours a year × ₹400 = ₹28.8 lakh. Total ₹1.08 crore a year.

USERS: Merchandisers, unit supervisors (update from the floor), and buyers' sourcing staff (read-only). The Managing Director signs the deal.

THE ASK: I find out an order is late when it is too late to save it. Supervisors should enter real numbers from the floor every day on their phones, in Tamil if they like. Every order should show green, amber or red against plan. Buyers should see progress without emailing us, and we need warnings two weeks early, not two days.

MUST HAVE:
- Order setup with PO, style, colour and size quantities, ex-factory date, and TNA milestones from a template
- Supervisor mobile update: daily quantity per stage, photo, and issue note by text or voice
- Order board with green, amber or red status, filtered by buyer, unit and ship week
- Delay warning from current daily output against remaining quantity and days left
- Buyer view of their own orders' milestones and photos
- Weekly status export per buyer (PDF or Excel)

CORE BUILD: Software Engineering candidates must ship this slice end to end, in about 6 to 8 screens: order setup with TNA milestones, supervisor daily update, order board with status colours, delay warning, and read-only buyer link. Roles: merchandiser and supervisor. AI: reason category from Tamil notes. Hard part: run-rate delay projection. Mock payments, messages and outside systems, and seed from the sample data. The rest of MUST HAVE is optional depth.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Costing, invoicing and export documents
- Fabric inventory
- Worker attendance and payroll

AI OR AUTOMATION: The delay warning is a run-rate calculation that shows its maths (pieces needed per day vs made per day). AI turns Tamil text or voice notes into an English reason category. When it is wrong: the original note sits beside the translation, merchandisers can change the category, and warnings reach buyers only after a merchandiser confirms them.

CONSTRAINTS: One buyer must never see another's styles or volumes. Supervisors use cheap phones with 2–3 GB RAM and patchy network, so updates must queue offline. Tamil interface. Buyers' compliance teams want a history of every date change.

DESIGN: The client values good, minimal design: clean layouts, white space, a restrained palette and clear type, with nothing on screen that lacks a purpose. Design counts as much as features. The order board must show which orders are in trouble at a glance; the supervisor screen needs only numbers, a photo and a send button.

BUDGET AND TIME: ₹7 lakh, 6 weeks. Success: late shipments from 8% to 5% over two seasons; status-chasing time halved; buyer status emails down 60%.

items.title: Jewellery chain's karigar gold ledger and old-gold desk app
items.body:
CLIENT: Company A, Coimbatore. Jewellery chain of 5 showrooms with its own workshop and about 40 karigars (goldsmiths). 180 staff, revenue ₹220–260 crore a year.

TODAY: Gold issued to karigars is written in a paper ledger and copied to Excel. A clerk works out wastage by hand when pieces, scrap and filings come back. Old gold bought from customers is tested on a karat meter and recorded on paper and in the billing software. Month-end reconciliation takes 6 people 3 days. Accounts run in Tally.

THE PROBLEM: Assumptions: 20 kg of fine gold issued a month, 240 kg a year. Loss beyond agreed wastage that nobody can explain: 0.4%, or 960 g. At ₹12,500 per gram (assumed rate), that is ₹1.2 crore. Reconciliation: 6 people × 3 days × 12 months = 216 person-days × ₹2,500 = ₹5.4 lakh. Total ₹1.25 crore a year.

USERS: The workshop manager and issue clerk, karigars (see slips on phone), and the finance head. The managing partner signs the deal.

THE ASK: Every gram that leaves my vault must come back as jewellery, scrap or an agreed allowance, and I want to see that per karigar on any day. Old gold from customers must be recorded once and tied to the bill. Tell me when a karigar's loss is rising, before month-end.

MUST HAVE:
- Karigar master with agreed wastage % per item category
- Issue entry: gross weight, purity, fine weight and job number, with a slip to the karigar and a running fine-gold balance
- Receipt entry for finished pieces (net weight, HUID), scrap and filings, with allowed vs actual wastage calculated
- Old gold desk: weight, tested purity, deductions, fine weight and value, linked to the exchange bill
- Loss alerts, and a daily stock statement of gold in vault, with karigars and at the refiner, with Tally export
- Karigar view of slips and balances on phone

CORE BUILD: Software Engineering candidates must ship this slice end to end, in about 6 to 8 screens: karigar master, issue and receipt entries with wastage maths, running balances, loss alerts, and daily stock statement. Roles: issue clerk and finance head. AI: reading scale photos. Hard part: exact fine-gold maths to 3 decimals. Mock payments, messages and outside systems, and seed from the sample data. The rest of MUST HAVE is optional depth.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Replacing the showroom billing software
- Customer app or gold savings schemes
- Gold loans

AI OR AUTOMATION: AI reads photos of the scale display or karat meter printout to fill weight and purity, and flags karigars whose loss drifts from their own history. When AI is wrong: each reading appears beside its photo for the clerk to confirm, and a mismatch with a typed value blocks saving. Loss alerts go only to the finance head and partner as items to review, never as accusations.

CONSTRAINTS: Weights to 3 decimals, purity to 2. Record PAN and payment mode on high-value old-gold purchases for income tax cash limits. Stock data is owner-only. Karigars read Tamil. Shared tablets must cope with power and network cuts.

DESIGN: The client values good, minimal design: clean layouts, white space, a restrained palette and clear type, with nothing on screen that lacks a purpose. Design counts as much as features. Gold figures must be easy to read and hard to misread: clear numerals, aligned decimals and balances that stand out.

BUDGET AND TIME: ₹6 lakh, 6 weeks. Success: unexplained loss from 0.4% to under 0.15%; month-end reconciliation from 3 days to half a day.

items.title: D2C home brand's order, payment and return reconciliation tool
items.body:
CLIENT: Company A, Bengaluru. D2C home textiles brand selling on its own website, 3 marketplaces and 2 quick-commerce apps. 45 staff, revenue ₹38–45 crore a year, a finance team of 3.

TODAY: Shipping runs through 2 courier aggregators, and 55% of website orders are cash on delivery (COD). Each month finance downloads settlement, COD remittance and freight invoice reports into Excel and matches them with lookups. Returns are rarely checked against what reached the warehouse. Books are in Tally.

THE PROBLEM: Assumptions: 30,000 orders a month at ₹1,200 average, ₹43.2 crore a year. 1.5% of order value leaks through unremitted COD, wrong fees, wrong weight slabs and lost returns: ₹64.8 lakh. Finance spends 60% of its time reconciling: 3 × 60% × ₹6 lakh = ₹10.8 lakh. Total ₹75.6 lakh a year, and month-end close takes 12 days.

USERS: Finance executives, the returns manager, and the finance co-founder, who signs the deal.

THE ASK: We know money is leaking but we can't say where. I want to upload every partner's reports and see, per order, whether we were paid the right amount. Anything short, late or overcharged should land in a claims list with evidence. Returns that never arrived must be caught within days.

MUST HAVE:
- Upload of order, settlement, COD and freight files (CSV or Excel) with column mapping saved per source
- Order-level matching with statuses: settled, short-paid, unpaid past due, freight overcharged, return not received
- Rate cards per channel and courier to compute expected amounts and flag gaps over ₹10
- Returns tracker against warehouse receipt scans
- Claims list by partner with evidence export, and a money-at-risk dashboard by partner and age
- Partner-wise summary of TCS and TDS deducted

CORE BUILD: Software Engineering candidates must ship this slice end to end, in about 6 to 8 screens: file upload with saved column mapping, order-level matching, rate-card expected amounts, claims list, and money-at-risk view. Roles: finance executive and co-founder. AI: column mapping suggestions. Hard part: matching 1 lakh rows in under a minute. Mock payments, messages and outside systems, and seed from the sample data. The rest of MUST HAVE is optional depth.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Storefront or inventory sync
- GST filing
- Automatic claim filing

AI OR AUTOMATION: Matching and expected amounts are rules, not AI. AI proposes column mappings when a partner changes its format, and suggests matches when an order ID is missing. When it is wrong: mappings are previewed on 20 rows, approved before saving, and versioned for rollback. Suggested matches go to a review queue and are never closed automatically.

CONSTRAINTS: Customer names, phones and addresses are personal data under the DPDP Act 2023, so mask them where not needed. Settlements deduct GST TCS and income tax TDS, which must be shown separately, not as leakage. Files of 1 lakh rows should process in under a minute. Formats change without notice.

DESIGN: The client values good, minimal design: clean layouts, white space, a restrained palette and clear type, with nothing on screen that lacks a purpose. Design counts as much as features. Finance staff work through large tables: make differences and money at risk stand out, and keep filters simple.

BUDGET AND TIME: ₹6.5 lakh, 6 weeks. Success: 98% of orders auto-matched; month-end close from 12 days to 3; at least ₹30 lakh recovered through claims in year one.

items.title: FMCG distributor's retailer ordering app with AI order capture
items.body:
CLIENT: Company A, Jabalpur. Distributor for 4 packaged food and home care brands, serving 1,800 kirana shops. 70 staff including 18 salesmen, revenue ₹85–100 crore a year.

TODAY: Salesmen write orders in notebooks, or retailers send WhatsApp texts, photos of handwritten lists and Hindi voice notes. Next morning an office team of 6 types them into Tally. Salesmen don't know stock or schemes at the counter, so lines are cut later.

THE PROBLEM: Assumptions: 600 orders a day, 300 days, ₹5,000 per order, so ₹90 crore a year. 5% of orders have a wrong item or quantity needing a return or redelivery: 1,80,000 × 5% = 9,000 × ₹350 = ₹31.5 lakh. Order entry staff: 6 × ₹2.6 lakh = ₹15.6 lakh. Stock-outs found after ordering lose 1% of sales at 6% margin: ₹90 lakh × 6% = ₹5.4 lakh. Total ₹52.5 lakh a year.

USERS: Retailers (shop owners on phones), salesmen, and the office order desk. The owner-director signs the deal.

THE ASK: My shopkeepers already order on WhatsApp, each in their own way, and my office retypes it all. I want a simple app where a retailer sees stock, his price and the current scheme, and orders in a minute. Salesmen should use it in the shop, even without signal. Messages and voice notes should become orders my desk only has to check.

MUST HAVE:
- Installable web app with OTP login, catalogue, retailer prices and schemes, stock status, repeat order and credit limit
- Salesman mode for orders during visits, working offline
- AI order capture from text, a photo of a list, or a Hindi voice note
- Scheme engine for free goods (buy 10 get 1) and slab discounts
- Order desk with credit holds, Tally export and van loading lists
- Dashboard of retailers with no order in 14 days

CORE BUILD: Software Engineering candidates must ship this slice end to end, in about 6 to 8 screens: retailer catalogue with prices and schemes, cart and order, AI capture from a text order, and order desk with Tally export. Roles: retailer and order desk. AI: order capture from messages. Hard part: the scheme engine. Mock payments, messages and outside systems, and seed from the sample data. The rest of MUST HAVE is optional depth.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Delivery tracking
- Payments in the app
- GST e-invoicing (stays in Tally)

AI OR AUTOMATION: AI reads text, photos and voice notes and maps items to SKUs using the retailer's past orders. When it is wrong: each line shows the original words, a confidence level and two alternative SKUs, and unclear units (case or piece) are asked, not guessed. No order is placed until a person confirms it, and desk corrections become aliases for that retailer.

CONSTRAINTS: Retailers use low-end phones on slow 3G: first load under 3 seconds, large tap targets. Hindi and English. Prices must show clearly whether GST is included. A retailer's prices and credit are visible only to them, their salesman and the desk.

DESIGN: The client values good, minimal design: clean layouts, white space, a restrained palette and clear type, with nothing on screen that lacks a purpose. Design counts as much as features. Shopkeepers order between customers: a fast, uncluttered catalogue with large images, clear prices and a quick cart.

BUDGET AND TIME: ₹7 lakh, 6 weeks. Success: 50% of orders placed in the app or captured by AI in 4 months; orders with errors from 5% to under 1%; order entry team from 6 to 3.

items.title: Road transport fleet's proof-of-delivery capture and billing app
items.body:
CLIENT: Company A, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Maharashtra. Full-truckload transporter for cement, steel and packaged goods firms. 140 own trucks plus about 200 hired ones, 210 staff, revenue ₹75–90 crore a year.

TODAY: Drivers bring the signed lorry receipt (LR) or proof of delivery (POD) back after the trip, often 10–20 days later. Photos sent on WhatsApp get lost. Billing in Tally waits for the POD, as clients reject invoices without one.

THE PROBLEM: Assumptions: 2,200 trips a month at ₹32,000 average freight, ₹84.48 crore a year. POD-to-invoice takes 18 days; cutting it to 4 days brings billing 14 days forward: ₹84.48 crore × 14 / 365 = ₹3.24 crore of working capital, costing ₹38.9 lakh a year at 12% interest. 1.5% of PODs (396 trips a year) are lost or disputed, losing half the freight: 396 × ₹16,000 = ₹63.36 lakh. Total ₹1.02 crore a year.

USERS: Drivers (basic phones, low literacy), billing executives, and the operations head. The Managing Director signs the deal.

THE ASK: I can't bill until a piece of paper comes back from 800 km away. I want the driver to take a photo at the consignee's gate and be done. The system should check the photo while the driver is still there.

MUST HAVE:
- Driver app with one big button to photograph the POD, stamped with GPS and time
- SMS upload link for hired drivers who won't install an app
- AI POD check of LR number, consignee stamp, quantity, shortage or damage remarks, date and signature, asking for a retake if needed
- Billing queue of verified trips by client and cycle, with Tally export and POD images attached to invoices
- Dashboard of trips without POD and POD-to-invoice days by branch, plus a client link to view PODs
- Daily trip import with LR and e-way bill numbers

CORE BUILD: Software Engineering candidates must ship this slice end to end, in about 6 to 8 screens: driver POD capture, AI check with retake prompt, review queue, billing queue with export, and missing-POD dashboard. Roles: driver and billing executive. AI: POD photo check. Hard part: offline capture with compressed upload. Mock payments, messages and outside systems, and seed from the sample data. The rest of MUST HAVE is optional depth.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Live GPS tracking
- Trip planning
- Fuel and driver expense accounting

AI OR AUTOMATION: A vision AI model checks each POD photo and extracts fields. When it is wrong: the image stays the source of truth; any POD with a shortage or damage remark, or low confidence, goes to a billing executive, who can correct fields; invoices are never sent automatically. Retakes are capped at two.

CONSTRAINTS: Each trip links to its e-way bill. Drivers need icons and Hindi or Marathi voice prompts, not typing. Highways have dead zones, so capture works offline and images are compressed under 300 KB. Consignee names and phones are personal data under the DPDP Act 2023.

DESIGN: The client values good, minimal design: clean layouts, white space, a restrained palette and clear type, with nothing on screen that lacks a purpose. Design counts as much as features. Many drivers do not read well: one big button, icons, a clear colour for success or retake, and no forms.

BUDGET AND TIME: ₹7.5 lakh, 6 weeks. Success: 80% of PODs in the system within 24 hours of delivery; POD-to-invoice from 18 days to 4; lost or disputed PODs from 1.5% to 0.5%.

items.title: Hill resort's direct-booking website with AI enquiry routing
items.body:
CLIENT: Company A, Chikkamagaluru, Karnataka. Coffee-estate resort with 64 rooms and 12 villas (76 keys) and lawns for weddings and offsites. 140 staff, revenue ₹24–28 crore a year. Run by a General Manager (GM).

TODAY: 68% of room nights come through online travel agencies at 18–22% commission; only 12% are direct. The website is a brochure with a phone number. Event enquiries arrive by email, phone, social media and the GM's own WhatsApp. Rates live in Excel.

THE PROBLEM: Assumptions: 76 keys × 365 × 62% occupancy = 17,199 room nights at ₹9,500. 68% via agencies = 11,695 nights = ₹11.11 crore, at 20% commission = ₹2.22 crore a year; moving 15% of that to direct saves ₹33.3 lakh. Of 90 event enquiries a month, 30% wait over a day for a reply, losing about 3 events a month at ₹2 lakh contribution: 36 × ₹2 lakh = ₹72 lakh. Total ₹1.05 crore a year.

USERS: Guests, the reservations and sales team, and the GM. The owner signs the deal.

THE ASK: We pay agencies a fifth of every room they sell, while many guests would book direct if our site let them. I want a fast, beautiful site where guests pick dates, see real prices and pay. Every enquiry, from any channel, should land in one place and reach the right person with a reply ready.

MUST HAVE:
- Booking website: rooms with photos, availability, rate plans, prices with taxes, test-mode payment and confirmation
- Admin for daily rates, website allotment, blackout dates and promo codes
- One enquiry inbox for the web form, forwarded emails and WhatsApp (simulated in this build)
- AI router: classifies enquiries (room, wedding, offsite, complaint), extracts dates, guests and budget, assigns an owner and drafts a reply
- Structured wedding and event enquiry form
- Daily booking export for the reservation system

CORE BUILD: Software Engineering candidates must ship this slice end to end, in about 6 to 8 screens: room pages with availability and price, booking with test payment, rate and allotment admin, and enquiry inbox with AI routing. Roles: guest and reservations staff. AI: enquiry classification and reply draft. Hard part: allotment control so the site never overbooks. Mock payments, messages and outside systems, and seed from the sample data. The rest of MUST HAVE is optional depth.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Replacing the reservation system or a channel manager
- Loyalty programme
- Restaurant bookings

AI OR AUTOMATION: AI classifies, routes and drafts replies. When it is wrong: low-confidence enquiries go to an unsorted lane the GM sees; staff re-route in one click; drafts are never sent automatically; prices in drafts come from the rate table, not the AI. Complaints always alert the GM.

CONSTRAINTS: The site sells only an admin-set allotment, so it cannot overbook agency stock. Passport details for foreign guests' Form C are taken at check-in, not online. Guest data is personal data under the DPDP Act 2023. Pages and photos must load fast on slow hill-station networks. Show GST at the rate for the tariff.

DESIGN: The client values good, minimal design: clean layouts, white space, a restrained palette and clear type, with nothing on screen that lacks a purpose. Design counts as much as features. The booking site sells the experience: large photos, a quiet layout and a booking flow of no more than three steps.

BUDGET AND TIME: ₹8 lakh, 7 weeks. Success: direct share from 12% to 20% of room nights in 12 months; median first reply under 30 minutes in working hours; zero website overbookings.

items.title: Staffing firm's AI resume screening tool and client shortlist portal
items.body:
CLIENT: Company A, Noida. Contract and permanent hiring for IT services, banking back-office and retail clients. 120 staff including 70 recruiters, revenue ₹40–50 crore a year.

TODAY: Clients email job descriptions (JDs). Recruiters search job boards and an old internal database, download CVs and read each one. Shortlists go to clients as Excel sheets with CVs attached. Feedback comes by email or phone, and status lives in each recruiter's own sheet.

THE PROBLEM: Assumptions: 300 open requisitions a month, 120 CVs each, 3 minutes per CV. 300 × 120 × 3 = 1,08,000 minutes = 1,800 hours a month, 21,600 hours a year × ₹350 = ₹75.6 lakh. Shortlists take 5 days, and 5% of requisitions (180 of 3,600 a year) are lost to faster rivals at ₹45,000 average fee: ₹81 lakh. Total ₹1.57 crore a year.

USERS: Recruiters, client hiring managers, and the delivery head. The CEO signs the deal.

THE ASK: My recruiters spend their day reading CVs that were never going to fit. I want them to upload a pile of CVs against a job and see the best first, with reasons. Clients should review shortlists in a portal, not by phone. I must be able to show clients that we treat candidates fairly.

MUST HAVE:
- JD intake: AI extracts must-have skills, experience, CTC and notice into an editable scorecard
- Bulk CV upload (PDF or DOCX, up to 500), parsed into profiles with duplicate detection
- AI score per CV with evidence lines quoted from the CV for each criterion
- Client portal with masked contacts, where clients shortlist, reject with a reason or propose an interview slot
- Pipeline per requisition from sourced to joined
- Candidate consent record and deletion on request

CORE BUILD: Software Engineering candidates must ship this slice end to end, in about 6 to 8 screens: JD scorecard, bulk CV upload and parsing, ranked list with evidence, client shortlist portal, and pipeline. Roles: recruiter and client hiring manager. AI: CV scoring with evidence. Hard part: parsing varied CV formats in bulk. Mock payments, messages and outside systems, and seed from the sample data. The rest of MUST HAVE is optional depth.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Job board integrations or scraping
- Video interviews
- Background verification

AI OR AUTOMATION: AI parses CVs and scores them against the scorecard. When it is wrong: it never rejects anyone automatically; every score shows its evidence; a recruiter must open a CV before submitting it; name, gender, age, photo and marital status are hidden from scoring; low scorers stay searchable. A weekly sample compares AI ranks with recruiter choices for the delivery head.

CONSTRAINTS: CVs are personal data under the DPDP Act 2023: consent, hiring use only, deletion on request, and a log of who viewed what. Each client sees only candidates submitted to them. Some CVs are scans; clients often review on phones.

DESIGN: The client values good, minimal design: clean layouts, white space, a restrained palette and clear type, with nothing on screen that lacks a purpose. Design counts as much as features. Recruiters scan many profiles: make the score, its evidence and the next action clear; the client portal should look clean and professional on a phone.

BUDGET AND TIME: ₹7 lakh, 6 weeks. Success: screening time per requisition down 60%; shortlist within 48 hours for 80% of requisitions; client acceptance of candidates from 45% to 60%.

items.title: Rooftop solar installer's lead qualification, quotation and project tracker
items.body:
CLIENT: Company A, Nagpur. Rooftop solar for homes and small businesses across Vidarbha. 75 staff, revenue ₹30–38 crore a year, about 120 installations a month.

TODAY: Leads land in WhatsApp and Excel. Sales calls every lead and asks for an electricity bill photo, then a surveyor visits the roof. Quotes are built in Excel. Subsidy applications and net metering with the electricity distribution company (DISCOM) are tracked in another sheet.

THE PROBLEM: Assumptions: 1,400 leads a month, 25% (350) genuine. 40% of 220 monthly surveys are for people who were never going to buy: 88 × ₹2,500 × 12 = ₹26.4 lakh a year. Quotes take 3 days, and 4% of genuine leads (14 a month) go to faster rivals at ₹2 lakh order value and 18% margin: 14 × ₹36,000 × 12 = ₹60.48 lakh. Total ₹86.88 lakh a year.

USERS: Homeowners (on phones), sales and survey staff, and the project coordinator. The founder-MD signs the deal.

THE ASK: Half my team's day goes on tenants and people with ₹600 bills. I want leads to answer a few questions and upload their bill, and the system to tell us who is worth a visit and what size fits. After the survey, the quote should go out the same day with subsidy and payback worked out.

MUST HAVE:
- Lead form: owner or tenant, roof type and area, monthly bill, pincode, bill photo
- AI bill reading of consumer number, tariff, sanctioned load and monthly units, giving a score and recommended system size
- Quote PDF with system options, yearly generation, subsidy, net cost and payback
- Project tracker from advance to subsidy credited, with documents and a customer status link
- WhatsApp or SMS update on each stage change, and a dashboard of stuck projects
- Admin tables for prices and subsidy rules with effective dates

CORE BUILD: Software Engineering candidates must ship this slice end to end, in about 6 to 8 screens: lead form with bill upload, AI bill reading and score, quote builder with subsidy and payback, and project tracker with status link. Roles: homeowner and sales staff. AI: bill reading and lead score. Hard part: subsidy and payback maths from dated rule tables. Mock payments, messages and outside systems, and seed from the sample data. The rest of MUST HAVE is optional depth.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Filing on the government subsidy portal
- Inventory and purchasing
- Inverter monitoring

AI OR AUTOMATION: AI reads bill photos and scores leads. When it is wrong: extracted values appear beside the bill image for confirmation; a poor photo triggers a re-upload; a low score never rejects a lead, it only replaces the survey visit with a short call. The client says the central residential scheme pays ₹30,000 per kW up to 2 kW plus ₹18,000 for the third, capped at ₹78,000; verify before launch. Consumer numbers and addresses are personal data under the DPDP Act 2023. Marathi and Hindi.

DESIGN: The client values good, minimal design: clean layouts, white space, a restrained palette and clear type, with nothing on screen that lacks a purpose. Design counts as much as features. Homeowners should see the quote as a simple story: system size, cost after subsidy and payback, before any detail.

BUDGET AND TIME: ₹6 lakh, 6 weeks. Success: unqualified surveys from 40% to under 15%; same-day quotes for 90% of surveys; status calls down 50%.

items.title: Car dealership's end-to-end website with stock, test-drive and service booking
items.body:
CLIENT: Company A, Lucknow. Authorised dealer for one passenger car brand (called Brand X here) with 3 showrooms, 2 service workshops and a certified used-car yard. 340 staff, revenue ₹550–650 crore a year, about 6,000 new and 900 used cars sold a year.

TODAY: The website is a basic template with an enquiry form. Leads from the site, car portals, social ads and walk-ins are tracked in Excel; billing runs in the brand's dealer management system (DMS). Test drives and service bookings are fixed by phone. Used-car stock is shared as WhatsApp photos.

THE PROBLEM: Assumptions: 4,500 online leads a month. 30% (1,350) are not called within 24 hours and convert at 2% instead of 6%: 1,350 × 4% = 54 cars lost a month × ₹25,000 dealer contribution = ₹13.5 lakh a month, ₹1.62 crore a year. Of 3,000 service calls a month, 20% (600) go unanswered and half of those owners (300) go elsewhere: 300 × ₹4,500 average bill × 30% margin = ₹4.05 lakh a month, ₹48.6 lakh a year. Total ₹2.11 crore a year.

USERS: Car buyers and owners (mostly mobile), sales consultants and the lead desk, and service advisors. The Dealer Principal signs the deal.

THE ASK: Our website looks like every other dealer's and does nothing. I want buyers to browse new and used cars with real prices, see the on-road price and EMI, and book a test drive in a real slot without calling. Owners should book a service in a minute. Every enquiry should reach a named consultant within five minutes.

MUST HAVE:
- Model and variant pages: photos, specs, colours, ex-showroom and on-road price by city (road tax, insurance, accessories) from an admin price table
- Certified used-car listings with filters, photos, inspection report and price
- Test-drive booking by showroom and demo car, and service booking by workshop bay capacity
- EMI calculator and trade-in request form
- Lead inbox for web enquiries and portal CSV imports, auto-assigned by showroom and model, with a response timer and status
- Admin CMS for models, prices, offers, used stock, banners and user roles

CORE BUILD: Software Engineering candidates must ship this slice end to end, in about 6 to 8 screens: model and used-car pages with on-road price, test-drive booking, lead inbox with auto-assignment, and admin for cars and prices. Roles: buyer and sales consultant. AI: buyer summary and first-reply draft. Hard part: on-road price breakup by city from admin tables. Mock payments, messages and outside systems, and seed from the sample data. The rest of MUST HAVE is optional depth.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Online payment of booking amounts
- DMS integration (a daily CSV export instead)
- Spare parts e-commerce

AI OR AUTOMATION: Leads are assigned and acknowledged automatically by WhatsApp or SMS template. AI summarises each buyer's needs, drafts a first reply, and suggests a price band for used cars from past sales of the same model, year and kilometres. When it is wrong: drafts are edited before sending and never quote discounts; the used-car manager sets every final price and is the only one who sees the suggestion; consultants can re-assign leads; on-road prices always come from the admin table.

CONSTRAINTS: On-road prices must show the breakup, a validity date and a note that prices may change. Used-car listings show year, owners and kilometres but mask the full registration number. Buyer data is personal data under the DPDP Act 2023: consent checkbox and opt-out. Hindi and English. Pages must load in under 2.5 seconds on 4G, and every model and used car needs its own indexable page for search.

DESIGN: The client values good, minimal design: clean layouts, white space, a restrained palette and clear type, with nothing on screen that lacks a purpose. Design counts as much as features. The site should feel like a premium showroom: large car photography, generous spacing, one accent colour, and a price and a clear next step on every car page.

BUDGET AND TIME: ₹9 lakh, 8 weeks. Success: 90% of web leads called within 5 minutes; 400 online test-drive bookings a month within 6 months; unanswered service calls from 20% to under 5%.

items.title: NGO's donation platform with a women's schemes finder on the home page
items.body:
CLIENT: Company A, Bhopal. A registered charitable trust working on women's livelihoods and health in 9 districts of Madhya Pradesh. 220 staff, 1,400 volunteers, yearly budget ₹38–45 crore, mostly from CSR and grants.

TODAY: Donors pay by payment link, bank transfer or cheque. Receipts and 80G certificates are made in Word, and donors are kept in Excel. Form 10BD is compiled by hand. Women learn of schemes from leaflets and WhatsApp forwards, and call the helpline to ask what they qualify for.

THE PROBLEM: Assumptions: 12,000 donors give ₹6 crore a year (₹5,000 each on average) across 18,000 donations. Receipting takes 10 minutes each: 18,000 × 10 minutes = 3,000 hours × ₹300 = ₹9 lakh. Only 22% of donors give again next year; the target is 32%: 10% × 12,000 = 1,200 donors × ₹5,000 = ₹60 lakh. Helpline: 2,500 scheme calls a month × 8 minutes = 4,000 hours a year × ₹250 = ₹10 lakh. Total ₹79 lakh a year.

USERS: Women and field workers looking up schemes (mobile, Hindi), donors, and trust staff. The CEO signs the deal with board approval.

THE ASK: Our home page should first show women the schemes they can use, in plain Hindi. Donors should give in two minutes, get their receipt and 80G certificate at once, and be able to give every month. My accounts team should never type a receipt again. It must hold up when a campaign brings thousands of donors in a day.

MUST HAVE:
- Home page led by a women's schemes section: browse by need and district; each scheme shows benefits, documents, how to apply and the nearest help centre
- Eligibility finder: 5–6 simple questions returning matching schemes
- Donation flow: one-time and monthly (test mode), campaign pages, PAN capture, instant receipt and 80G certificate
- Donor account with history and certificates
- Admin CMS for schemes, campaigns and pages in Hindi and English, with review before publish
- Accounts reports by campaign, with a Form 10BD export

CORE BUILD: Software Engineering candidates must ship this slice end to end, in about 6 to 8 screens: home page schemes section with eligibility finder, scheme admin, donation flow with test payment, and instant 80G receipt PDF. Roles: visitor or donor, and trust admin. AI: Hindi scheme summary drafts. Hard part: correct receipt numbering and 80G PDFs under load. Mock payments, messages and outside systems, and seed from the sample data. The rest of MUST HAVE is optional depth.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Foreign contributions (FCRA) online in this phase
- Volunteer management
- CSR and grant proposal tracking

AI OR AUTOMATION: Receipts, certificates and reminders are automated. AI drafts a plain Hindi summary of each scheme from its official notice, and lets the finder take a question typed or spoken in Hindi. When it is wrong: summaries are drafts that an editor must approve; each scheme page links to its official source and shows its last-checked date; finder results show possible matches with the rules used, never a promise, and offer a helpline call-back.

CONSTRAINTS: 80G certificates must carry the trust's PAN and 80G registration number and the donor's name, PAN and amount. Foreign cards are blocked with a notice, as foreign money needs an FCRA account. Donor and beneficiary data falls under the DPDP Act 2023; scheme pages carry no ad trackers. Hindi first, WCAG 2.1 AA, usable on low-end phones on 3G. Campaign days bring up to 5,000 donations in a few hours.

DESIGN: The client values good, minimal design: clean layouts, white space, a restrained palette and clear type, with nothing on screen that lacks a purpose. Design counts as much as features. The home page must feel warm, respectful and simple on a cheap phone: large Hindi type, plain icons, few choices per screen and no stock-photo clutter. Donating should take three steps at most.

BUDGET AND TIME: ₹9 lakh, 8 weeks. Success: no manual receipts; donor retention from 22% to 32% in 12 months; 50,000 finder uses in year one; helpline scheme calls down 40%.

items.title: Multi-campus college ERP for admissions, attendance, marks and fees
items.body:
CLIENT: Company A, Bhubaneswar. An educational trust running 3 campuses: an engineering college, a management school and a pharmacy college. 7,800 students, 520 teaching and 340 non-teaching staff, fee revenue ₹95–110 crore a year.

TODAY: Admissions run on Excel and online forms. Each campus keeps student records in a 12-year-old desktop program. Attendance is on paper, typed into Excel weekly; marks live in department sheets. Fees are paid at a bank counter and matched by hand in Tally. Staff leave is on paper. Reports for the university, AICTE and NAAC are compiled by hand.

THE PROBLEM: Assumptions: digital attendance and marks save each teacher 1 hour a week: 520 × 1 × 40 teaching weeks = 20,800 hours × ₹600 = ₹1.248 crore. 24 office staff spend 40% of their time re-entering data and building reports: 24 × 40% × ₹3.6 lakh = ₹34.56 lakh. Total ₹1.59 crore a year.

USERS: Faculty, students and parents (mobile), and office staff for admissions, exams, accounts and HR. The trust's Secretary signs the deal.

THE ASK: We run three colleges on paper, Excel and a desktop program nobody can fix. I want one system where a student exists once, from admission to graduation. Teachers should take attendance on their phones in class and enter marks once. Parents should see attendance and dues. When the university or NAAC asks for data, I want a report, not a two-week exercise.

MUST HAVE:
- Masters for campuses, programmes, batches, subjects, faculty and the calendar, with roles per campus
- Admission to student record: applicant import, document checklist, confirmation and roll numbers
- Period-wise attendance on mobile, working offline in class, with alerts below 75%
- Internal marks by component, moderation lock, mark sheets and export in the university upload format
- Fees: structures by programme and category, scholarships, payment link (test mode), receipts, dues and Tally export
- Staff leave, and dashboards per campus and for the trust

CORE BUILD: Software Engineering candidates must ship this slice end to end, in about 6 to 8 screens: one campus only: masters for one programme, mobile attendance, internal marks with moderation lock, and fee dues. Roles: faculty and office admin. AI: at-risk student flag. Hard part: offline attendance in class with sync. Mock payments, messages and outside systems, and seed from the sample data. The rest of MUST HAVE is optional depth.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Timetable generation
- Payroll
- Hostel, transport and library

AI OR AUTOMATION: Shortage alerts, fee reminders and standard reports run automatically. AI flags students at risk from attendance and marks trends, and lets office staff ask questions in plain English, such as how many second-year students are below 75% this month, by generating a read-only query. When it is wrong: the assistant shows the filters it used and the row count, runs only read-only queries on data the user's role may see, and cannot change records. At-risk flags only create a mentor task. Attendance and marks rules are fixed settings, not AI.

CONSTRAINTS: Student and parent data falls under the DPDP Act 2023; some first-year students are minors needing parental consent. Access is limited by campus and department. Marks lock after moderation and every change is logged for exam audits. Reports must match university, AICTE and NAAC formats. Results day brings 7,800 students at once. Classrooms have weak Wi-Fi. English, with Odia for parent messages.

DESIGN: The client values good, minimal design: clean layouts, white space, a restrained palette and clear type, with nothing on screen that lacks a purpose. Design counts as much as features. An ERP is used all day by hundreds of people, so calm, consistent screens matter most: one layout pattern across modules, clear tables, short menus, and attendance marked in under 30 seconds per class.

BUDGET AND TIME: ₹9 lakh, 8 weeks for this first phase. Success: attendance entered the same day for 95% of classes; university mark uploads with no re-typing; monthly fee reconciliation from 10 days to 1.

items.title: Tour operator's website with custom CMS for packages, blogs and enquiries
items.body:
CLIENT: Company A, Kochi. Tour operator selling Kerala and South India holiday packages to families, honeymooners and foreign groups. 48 staff, revenue ₹28–34 crore a year, about 4,300 bookings a year across 60 packages.

TODAY: The website was built by a freelancer 6 years ago, and every package or price change costs ₹3,000 and 3 days. Blogs sit on a free blogging platform with no link to packages. Enquiries arrive by web form, chat, WhatsApp, email and phone, and are logged in Excel. Quotes are Word files saved as PDF.

THE PROBLEM: Assumptions: 2,400 web enquiries a month, 15% of which book. 25% (600) get a reply after 12 hours and convert at 7% instead of 15%: 600 × 8% = 48 bookings lost a month × ₹65,000 average package × 14% margin = ₹4.37 lakh a month, ₹52.42 lakh a year. 40 content changes a month × ₹3,000 = ₹14.4 lakh a year. Total ₹66.82 lakh a year.

USERS: Travellers (mostly mobile), consultants who handle enquiries, and content staff. The founder-MD signs the deal.

THE ASK: I want to add a package or change a price myself in five minutes without calling anyone. Our blogs should live on our own site and lead readers to the right package. Every enquiry, from any channel, should land in one admin inbox, go to a consultant and get a reply within the hour. The site must look as good as the places we sell.

MUST HAVE:
- Public site: destination and package pages with day-wise itinerary, inclusions, hotels, seasonal pricing, photos and map, plus search
- Package CMS: create, edit, duplicate, seasonal prices, schedule, preview and version history
- Blog CMS: rich editor with images, categories, SEO fields and related packages on each post
- Enquiry forms on every package and an admin inbox with status, assignment, notes and replies
- Quote builder from a package, sent as a branded PDF and link
- Admin, editor and consultant roles with an activity log

CORE BUILD: Software Engineering candidates must ship this slice end to end, in about 6 to 8 screens: public package pages, package CMS with seasonal prices and preview, enquiry form, and admin enquiry inbox. Roles: traveller and staff admin. AI: enquiry extraction and package suggestions. Hard part: versioned CMS with preview and server-rendered pages. Mock payments, messages and outside systems, and seed from the sample data. The rest of MUST HAVE is optional depth.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Online payment and live hotel or flight inventory
- Visa services
- Native mobile apps

AI OR AUTOMATION: Every enquiry gets an instant acknowledgement from a fixed template. AI extracts dates, travellers, destination and budget from each message, suggests the three best-fit packages and drafts a reply. When it is wrong: extracted fields sit beside the original message for correction; nothing is sent or published until a consultant or editor accepts it; prices in drafts come from the package price table, never from the AI.

CONSTRAINTS: Prices must state the per-person basis, twin sharing and GST. Traveller data is personal data under the DPDP Act 2023; WhatsApp follow-ups need consent. Search matters: server-rendered pages, clean URLs, a sitemap, and redirects from 140 old URLs. Pages must load in under 2.5 seconds on 4G. English now; Hindi and German later.

DESIGN: The client values good, minimal design: clean layouts, white space, a restrained palette and clear type, with nothing on screen that lacks a purpose. Design counts as much as features. Travel is sold by feeling: full-width photography, quiet type and one clear Enquire button on every package. The admin panel must be just as clean, so a non-technical editor can update a package without training.

BUDGET AND TIME: ₹8.5 lakh, 7 weeks. Success: package changes done in-house in under 10 minutes; 90% of enquiries answered within an hour in working hours; organic traffic up 40% in 9 months; enquiry-to-booking from 15% to 18%.

items.title: Gated township's resident app for maintenance, complaints and visitors
items.body:
CLIENT: Company A, Pune. Facility management company running a gated township of 2,400 apartments in 28 towers for its residents' federation. 180 on-site staff, managing a maintenance budget of ₹22–26 crore a year.

TODAY: Maintenance bills are made in Excel and emailed. Payments by cheque, transfer or UPI are matched by hand before entry in Tally. Complaints come by phone to the help desk and through 28 tower WhatsApp groups. Visitors are written in paper registers at 4 gates. The clubhouse and courts are booked on a shared spreadsheet.

THE PROBLEM: Assumptions: 2,400 flats × ₹7,500 a month = ₹21.6 crore billed a year. 3% is never collected: ₹64.8 lakh. 3 accounts staff spend 60% of their time matching payments: 3 × 60% × ₹4.8 lakh = ₹8.64 lakh. Of 1,800 complaints a month, 25% (450) are reopened, each costing 45 minutes at ₹250 an hour: 450 × 0.75 × ₹250 × 12 = ₹10.13 lakh. Total ₹83.57 lakh a year.

USERS: Residents (owners and tenants, mobile), help desk staff, and gate guards. The federation committee approves; the facility company's MD signs the deal.

THE ASK: Residents should pay maintenance, raise complaints and book the clubhouse from one app, and always see where a complaint stands. Guards should log visitors on a tablet, and residents should approve guests from their phones. Payments must match themselves. The committee wants a monthly report it can trust.

MUST HAVE:
- Resident app (installable web app): OTP login linked to a flat, family and tenant members, notices
- Maintenance billing by flat area and rate, late fees per bye-laws, online payment (test mode), bank statement matching, receipts and a ledger per flat
- Complaints with category, photo, auto-assignment, response timer, status updates and a rating on closure
- Gate visitor management: guard tablet entry with photo, resident approval and pre-approved guest codes
- Amenity booking with slots, rules and fees
- Committee dashboard: collections, dues ageing and complaint times

CORE BUILD: Software Engineering candidates must ship this slice end to end, in about 6 to 8 screens: resident login, maintenance bills with test payment, bank statement matching, complaints with assignment and status, and committee view. Roles: resident and help-desk staff. AI: complaint category and urgency. Hard part: payment matching from a bank CSV. Mock payments, messages and outside systems, and seed from the sample data. The rest of MUST HAVE is optional depth.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Accounting beyond maintenance (Tally stays)
- CCTV or boom-barrier hardware integration
- Classifieds or a marketplace

AI OR AUTOMATION: Bank statement rows are matched to flats by amount, reference and UPI ID. AI classifies free-text complaints by category and urgency and links duplicates (ten flats reporting the same lift). When it is wrong: unclear payments go to an accounts queue and are never posted to a flat automatically; the help desk can change a category in one tap; safety words such as fire, gas, lift stuck or shock always escalate to the duty manager by rule, whatever the AI says; duplicates are linked, never closed.

CONSTRAINTS: Resident data, visitor photos and phone numbers are personal data under the DPDP Act 2023: delete visitor photos after 90 days and show a notice at gates. Billing and late interest follow the society's bye-laws under Maharashtra cooperative law. Gate tablets must keep working through network drops. English, Marathi and Hindi. Most bills are paid in the first 10 days of a month.

DESIGN: The client values good, minimal design: clean layouts, white space, a restrained palette and clear type, with nothing on screen that lacks a purpose. Design counts as much as features. Residents open the app for seconds at a time: the home screen shows dues, open complaints and today's visitors, with every action within two taps. Guard screens need very large buttons and photos that read well at night.

BUDGET AND TIME: ₹9 lakh, 8 weeks. Success: on-time payments from 70% to 90% in 6 months; payment matching time down 80%; reopened complaints from 25% to under 8%.

items.title: Farmer producer company's offline procurement and payment app
items.body:
CLIENT: Company A, Latur, Maharashtra. Farmer producer company owned by 6,200 farmer members in 140 villages. It buys soybean and tur from members at 22 village collection centres and sells to processors. 60 staff, turnover ₹70–85 crore a year.

TODAY: Centre staff weigh produce, test moisture and write a paper slip. Slips reach the office weekly and are typed into Excel. Bank payments are prepared from Excel 10–15 days later. The day's price is announced on WhatsApp. Farmers call to ask when they will be paid.

THE PROBLEM: Assumptions: 45,000 purchases a year, 15,000 tonnes in total. 2% of slips (900) have an error in weight, moisture or bank details, each costing ₹1,500 to fix: ₹13.5 lakh. Slow payment pushes members to sell 10% of their produce (1,500 tonnes) to private traders, losing ₹2,500 margin a tonne: ₹37.5 lakh. 5 data entry staff × ₹3 lakh = ₹15 lakh. Total ₹66 lakh a year.

USERS: Collection centre operators (Android phones, Marathi), farmer members (basic phones), and the office team. The CEO signs the deal.

THE ASK: Farmers should get a digital slip by SMS the moment their produce is weighed, and their money within 48 hours. My centre staff should enter weight and moisture once, on a phone, even with no network. The office should see stock at every centre by evening and make bank payment files without typing. Every centre must use the same price on the same day.

MUST HAVE:
- Member registry: farmer ID, village, land, verified bank account
- Offline collection app: find member, crop, gross and tare weight, moisture, grade, rate of the day, net amount, and a Marathi SMS slip
- Daily price board per crop and grade, set centrally and pushed to all centres
- Payment run: approved purchases grouped into the bank's bulk payment file, with status per farmer
- Centre stock and truck dispatch, with weight loss tracking
- Dashboard of purchases, pending payments and stock

CORE BUILD: Software Engineering candidates must ship this slice end to end, in about 6 to 8 screens: member registry, offline collection entry with SMS slip, daily price board, and payment run file. Roles: centre operator and office manager. AI: reading scale and meter photos. Hard part: offline-first entry with tamper-proof sync. Mock payments, messages and outside systems, and seed from the sample data. The rest of MUST HAVE is optional depth.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Sales invoicing and GST returns (stay in Tally)
- Seed and fertiliser shop
- Credit to farmers

AI OR AUTOMATION: Deductions follow a fixed rule table. AI reads photos of the scale display and moisture meter to prefill values, and flags unusual entries: weight far beyond what the farmer's land could yield, the same farmer twice in an hour, or moisture readings too uniform at one centre. When it is wrong: prefilled values sit beside the photo for the operator to confirm, and a typed value that differs blocks saving; flagged entries hold the payment for the procurement manager's review but never cancel a purchase; the farmer's SMS shows every value so they can dispute it.

CONSTRAINTS: Do not store Aadhaar numbers. Farmer data falls under the DPDP Act 2023. Weights in kg to one decimal, money to the paisa. Centres lose network for hours, so entries queue offline with tamper-proof timestamps. Low-end Android phones with 2 GB RAM. Marathi interface and SMS. Payment files must match the bank's bulk upload format.

DESIGN: The client values good, minimal design: clean layouts, white space, a restrained palette and clear type, with nothing on screen that lacks a purpose. Design counts as much as features. Operators work fast in dusty sheds with a queue of farmers: one step per screen, large numerals, high contrast in sunlight and a clear summary before saving. The farmer's slip must be readable in five seconds.

BUDGET AND TIME: ₹7.5 lakh, 7 weeks. Success: payment time from 12 days to 2; slip errors from 2% to under 0.3%; produce sold to private traders halved within a season.
